newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian railway strike goes ahead despite talks.
newsitem.headline: Belgian railway strike goes ahead despite talks.

text.p: Two unions of Belgian railway workers will go ahead with a 24-hour strike in six provinces from 2000 GMT on Monday after a reconciliation meeting with management ended without agreement.

The action by the Christian and socialist unions is over dissatisfaction with management's information policy and fears that the "Horizon 2005" restructuring and investment plan for the NMBS/SNCB national railways company will result in job losses.
Under the plan, to be completed by 2005, SNCB is to be split up into autonomous units, which is to help it be profitable.
NMBS/SNCB said in a statement it could not understand the motives for the strike. It said it had hired nearly 900 workers in 1996-1997 and would hire another 4,000 before the year 2005.
The strike will affect rail traffic in the provinces of East and West Flanders, Liege, Luxembourg and Namur, and the Brabant region around the key city of Leuven.
The unions have also announced temporary strikes in other areas for April 22 and 25.
